Professor Griffith is incredible and brilliantly smart, she is very clearly an expert in the field and tries to make the material interesting and relevant to us as engineering prospects. She although seems salty about teaching CHEM 135? She makes a lot of condescending jokes during class if no one answers a question, and takes jabs at the fact that the students in the lecture are trying to go into engineering and don't have any interest in chemistry. She has very professional slides, and if you go to class you will do well. I think the tests were fair, and they are very generous with the curve, and VERY FAST at grading tests! It was impressive.

Professor Schech is brilliant and absolutely a sweetheart. She tries to make everything relevant to us, and is very receptive to questions and really wants her students to understand the material. She's great with emailing in a timely manner and the tests are very fair. Her PowerPoints can be a little dull, but that's also because I had to take the class and have no interest in the content of chemistry. I would highly recommend if you are nervous about the class.
Online homework is nothing like the exams, some of the slide presentations are rushed (too much information at once)
Exams are nothing like online homework, homework are around 3 hrs + , lectures are fast paced
Hated every moment. Exams are beyond college level making not sense. HW are dumb and long. Reviews are fake.

Griffith is extremely smart and knows what she's talking about. Chances are if you ask her any question she'll answer it with a good explanation. However, her lectures move pretty fast and it's pretty hard to keep up with her pace at times and her exams were extremely difficult compared to the already difficult HW but she does curve at the end of the semester. Overall I'd recommend Griffith for CHEM135.

The most boring and horrible professor I have ever seen. If you haven't taken AP Chem or reviewed chem in the past year you are screwed. The only way to learn in her class is to do the homework which takes forever if you don't know what you are doing. Lectures are extremely boring and are mostly filled with examples that tell you nothing about what will be on the homework. Please switch to another professor!! The only good thing was that her practice exams and her exams are the same format.

Pick anyone other than Mignerey for CHEM135. We have a homework software(ALEKS) that takes the whole day just to do. Not only that but her lectures are so boring, you rather just look at her posted slides and watch videos to get by. Don't rely on her practice exams that she provides, they not similar. All her exams are just calculations problems and more difficult than other chemistry professors like Griffith. Always take Griffith for CHEM135.
Terrible professor. Very uninteresting, makes the tests way too difficult, and quite frankly gets off topic too often. I would avoid at all costs.

Dr. Griffith is genuinely one of the best chemistry professors I have ever had. She is extremely caring and really wants her students to do well. She was always willing to work with me if I couldn't come to office hours or needed any help. I had a really bad TA so I mostly relied on her office hours to help me get through. She offers tons of in-class bonus points through clickers. Her lectures are a little fast, but she tries to give as many examples as possible and shows the derivation of each of the concepts so it is easy to understand where the formulas were coming from if I ever forgot one. Her lectures being fast also is not her fault at all there is just a lot of material that needs to be covered in the class. By no means is it an easy class, but she offers tons of help and support to make things a little easier.  We get to use a notecard on every exam and also on the final. She also provides an outline of every exam before and shows all of the point values and the concepts tested for each question.  The exams are difficult, but fair and she is willing to regrade for partial credit. If you stay on top of your assignments and ask for it if you need help you should be good. She is also redesigning her class right now which is making the material a lot more manageable. Overall, Griffith is a really great professor, and I would definitely recommend her class.

Dr. Griffith is great!! She records all of her lectures, always gives bonus clicker questions in class, and is always available to help out. She is a great teacher and definitely knowledgeable about chemistry. Her exams are hard but we get a decent-sized notecard and she tells us the outline of the exams with point values and the concepts tested so with that and all of the previous exams and keys it is not too hard to find the format of the questions. Obviously, like any teacher, she throws curveballs on her exams but she does give partial credit and is always willing to work with you if you need help. She also posts all of her lecture recordings which is really helpful to look back on. If you do the homework, show up to class, make a good discussion group, and ask her if you need help it is not a bad class. Definitely recommend Dr. Griffith!!!

Her lectures are not that helpful, but if you use the textbook, the class isn't nearly as bad as what other people say. Her teaching style is definitely not good, but she makes up for it with her exams that are very similar to her practice exam format, and she also gives a list of the exact topics you will need to know, which is also quite helpful for preparing for exams.

I absolutely hate chemistry and am only taking it to fulfil a requirement, but Dr. Schech is super nice and very good at explaining topics in chemistry that I had a hard time trying to understand prior. She posts all her lectures online which are very helpful when trying to review, and even cuts them down to make them shorter! She also posts past exams for midterms and the final which are very helpful! Right now, we are a bit behind and are rushing through the last few modules, the exams are difficult but if the class average goes too low she will curve, and the homework isn't really representative of everything we do in class or the exams, but the rest of the class is great! I'd defintely recommend taking Dr. Schech for CHEM135!

Mignerey is genuinely the worst teacher I have ever had in 13 years of schooling. There are so many complaints I don't know where to begin. For starters, her lectures are absolutely useless. Her lectures consist of her copying down her slides (which look like they were last updated in 2008), fiddling with tech that she doesn't know how to use, and making mistakes upon mistakes COPYING down her OWN work. She makes so many mistakes in her lectures that many students find it more useful to NOT attend her lectures and read the slides themselves. On top of her terrible, almost non-existent teaching skills, she assigns the most painfully tedious and boring homework. No joke, I have recorded almost 90+ hours on ALEKS (the homework software) which she also assigns over "break" and holidays. Her practice tests may be similar to the actual exams, but the exams themselves are created in ways as if it seems she wants the students to fail them. Additionally, for some reason she decides to have four midterms, the last of which is A WEEK before the final exam.  Although the TA tries, she is unable to makeup for the horrendous teaching practices of Mignerey, If you need to postpone taking chemistry for a semester I would STRONGLY recommend that over wasting a hundred hours on a teacher that doesn't even care about teaching her class.

Definitely not the professor you want for chem. If you are good at teaching yourself, then you'll be fine, but otherwise, I would recommend avoiding her.  Her lectures are just her flying through PowerPoints (too fast to write down notes) and talking about examples of topics that she barely even taught us, and the discussions didn't help much with that either. The only thing that I actually learned from were the homework assignments. The one good thing though is that she gives practice exams that are pretty similar to the actual exams, and she does have a decent curve at the end of the class. Also, she does grade very quick, so you don't have to worry about that. Overall, it was between a 2 and a 3, but I chose 2 just because of how confused I was taking her class. If you can get a better professor, go for it, but if you get her, its not the end of the world.

Avoid choosing this professor at all costs!  Her lectures are not that helpful, and the homework software (ALEKS) is not representative of the material on the test.  She assigns multiple (40 topics) that have 5 questions in each topic, you will be doing chemistry homework all night with little reward.  Yes ALEKS teaches you better than she does but the test looks nothing like the homework.  I HIGHLY recommend choosing another professor as this should be a VERY LAST RESORT, I would recommend dropping out before taking this class.  Practice exams are somewhat helpful but she makes multiple errors and is always correcting mistakes that others find.  Lastly, DO NOT TRUST the fake responses below saying she is amazing because they are just trying to boost her rating.
Great professor, so many opportunities of extra credit. Fair deadlines and exam content is clear. Posts old exams for practice that are very similar to those.

Mignerey is the worst teacher I have had in thirteen years of school. Her teaching style is nonexistent as the majority of her lectures consist of her failing to set up technology, copying down the slides, and making COUNTLESS mistakes. In fact, her lectures are so poor that the majority of students feel like its more beneficial to not attend and just look at the slides, as her narration makes concepts MORE confusing. On top of her terrible teaching she assigns hours of tedious homework as if this is the only class the students are taking. Although the homework software, ALEKS, does help students learn; it ends up taking 95 hours of your semester to complete (seriously  -- and she assigns work over break) . In addition to her terrible teaching and tedious homework Mignerey structures her class to have four midterms, the last of which is taken only one week prior to the final exam. These exams do not test your knowledge in the course as Mingerey randomly cobbles together niche topics from her slides. The only reason I was able to get an A in this class was because I put over 100 hours of self study time ( which is completely unnecessary when better teachers exist). DO NOT TAKE ALICE MIGNEREY, restructure your schedule if you need to.

Best CHEM135 professor!!! Allows us to vote on 3 questions for the final which are identical to one question from each of the midterms. Gives lots of bonus points during lectures. Lectures are recorded. Always helpful during office hours and email.

If you have to take CHEM135 at UMD then please take another professor. She teaches solely using half assed slide decks and never puts any effort into teaching in an engaging manner or in any manner that allows students to learn well. The practice exams she posts to review for the midterms are much easier than the actual midterms so you always go into tests feeling better than you should. On two tests this year there have been questions that were simply never covered in class. The homework software (ALEKS) that all students have to use is horrible and takes an ungodly amount of time ( I spent over a hundred hours just on homework this semester), and is the only way anyone actually ends up learning any content. PLEASE switch teachers if you have her or simply drop the class and take it another semester as it is simply not worth it. I would give her 0 stars if I could.

Very good teacher. She records all of her lectures, which includes her written notes + powerpoints. She provides plenty of resources in order to stay afloat in her class. The class did move at a very fast pace but she never assigned extra lecture videos or extra homework (I never took chemistry either so everything was brand new to me). Outside of class, I dedicated about 5-10 hours a week doing homework and rewatching lectures to understand the class work.  She really does want all of her students to do well. I really recommend her!

Lectures are so boring and unhelpful. She has a bunch of example problems that she'll go through each class, but she reads everything off the slides as if you already know it. The homework was tedious and took a ridiculously long time, but it was also the only way I learned anything in this class. She provides good study materials but I basically had to teach everything to myself. This class isn't hard if you take it with a different professor.

Great professor for Chem 135. Lectures are easy to follow along and she does a great job explaining the concepts and going through examples. All lectures are recorded and she uploads all lecture slides and handwritten notes to ELMS. HW assignments weren't bad and she gives a lot of points through clicker questions during lecture and offers bonus points as well. Tests were hard but she does curve the class and gives you a notecard to use during the test. She definitely made a notoriously difficult class a lot more digestible, and I would definitely recommend her.

Dr. Griffith is such a good professor! She is extremely personable and is so passionate about chemistry, and it shows in how she teaches and her attitude. However, this course was very hard for me. The magnitude of information you're expected to retain and the difficulty of those topics make this course very rigorous. However, if you keep up with the lectures, do practice problems on top of homework, and understand the module activities throughout the semester, you should be fine. She offers a lot of bonus extra credit and lots of advice and insight for her exams (like the layout and the topic of each question). She knows how difficult this course is and is constantly offering support and help, she wants you to succeed and she believes in you!! For the final, she let us vote on 3 questions we wanted from the midterms to be on the final, so those were guaranteed points. I would go to her office hours frequently, you can gain valuable insight from questions asked by other students as well and she's such a great person to talk to. Continuing this semester (Fall 2023), she and another professor are redesigning the course so you kind of jump around in the chapters in the textbook. She applies the actual chemistry to topics engineers will need to know later down the line (like combustion or corrosion). I also did not find discussions particularly useful. There are videos that Dr. Griffith recorded in a previous year that you have to watch before the discussion, then the TA basically reteaches it. Unfortunately, I did not have a good experience with the TA as he did not teach well at all, so I would definitely just watch the videos. Although I really don't like chemistry, I am overall happy and satisfied I took this class with Dr. Griffith!

Terrible professor. I wish I checked his reviews before taking this class. He assigns a quiz every week but doesn't prepare us for it or give us enough time to do it. Even worse, 90% of the time, out of the 20 multiple-choice possible answers he gives for one single question, NONE OF THEM ARE THE ACTUAL CORRECT ANSWER. His lectures are unclear and confusing and the way he answers questions is very condescending. The lecture videos and the modules are more helpful but contain errors and are not posted consistently. Nothing in his class prepares us for the exams. Worst of all, THERE ARE MISTAKES ON THE EXAMS. It's an app you connect to so you don't have to be in class to do it. Lectures are useless don't even bother going. 

Gave us an exam the day before thanksgiving break so everyone left and my section had to stay which was just really annoying. If you are good at teaching yourself then you will be fine.

Probably the best professor I've had so far. As long as you keep up with the content learned in lectures and the textbook, 135 is a pretty easy course. Collins is also really good at discussion. For an intro chem course, I would definitely recommend him.

Coming from someone who had no Bs in high school, this course is challenging. His presentations are filled with useless information and the majority of the time the information from lecture is not going to be on the exam. Must teach yourself, however his practice exams are sometimes useful and discussion can be helpful.

I LOVE Dr Griffith!! She is one of the few professors you can tell cares about her students. She is very undertanding and kind and willing to help. The class itself is hard but she makes it very easy for you to pass as long as you put time into it. Her TA is also very helpful and although the course is not curved there are many chances for bonus points. She is the reason I did not fully crashout this semester. LOVE HER

Professor Griffith is awesome. Griffith truly cares about her students and is easily the best chem teacher. Everyone else I talk to that isn't in her class is struggling due to the inherent difficulty of the course. Griffith gives you all the resources to succeed in her class. She records lectures, allows note cards on exams, and gives out a plethora of bonus points that bump your grade by a lot. She also always posts numerous practice exams that are very similar to the actual exams so if you look at those you should be fine. Chem 135 is a difficult class but if you take Griffith you'll be fine.

Dr.Griffith is an amazing teacher. When she teaches it is engaging and fun. She makes complex concepts easy to understand. The homework is great practice and the class content easily prepares you for it. During office hours Dr.Griffith is very nice and clearly explains questions. The textbook is also amazing by far the best I have read. It really does feel like she cares about teaching.

I would not take him. His lectures are hard to understand. He writes in super tiny print on his whiteboard when he decides to draw something. If you want to see what he writes, you have to sit in the first 4 rows. We have asked him to write bigger and he basically just told us off. He gets sassy when you ask him anything he doesn't feel like doing. Early in the semester, his microphone was way too quiet. We asked him to turn the volume up and he was so smug about it, despite how quietly he talked. He puts class statistics for the exams up on the projector, and basically points and laughs at the group of students who do not do well. I've asked him for help, and he basically just told me practice more. Despite this advice, his practice exams and actual exams are wildly different in difficulty level. I (and many others I have talked to) did very well on the third practice exam, whereas his actual exam (which was on the last day of classes before thanksgiving break) was much harder. The class average was a 55, and he applied a 5% curve because "nobody can have above an 100%". I was a high A student in high school (and have an A or A- in every other class I am in here). Best we can do is hope for a curve at the end of the semester. The only good thing about this class is a 10% curve built into the Syllabus. Unless you want to sit down and learn it all yourself, take Griffith. I crashed a few of her lectures and she seemed to actually care that her students understand the content. I think I learned more from her by crashing 3 of her lectures than I learned from Dr.Vedernikov. The worst part is if you have any technology problem you must "fix it yourself" as it is "not my grade". One time more than half the class was unable to connect to his "clicker questions" and he said to the class "it's not my problem that your devices are not connected". My favorite part about this "policy" is when he was unable to get it to work and instantly called the university technical support to come fix it for him. Either way, he does not come off as the type of professor that cares about his students. If you have to take him (at least for 135), make sure you stay caught up on the textbook, and be ready for the "clicker questions" to be a complete curve-ball. Either way, you get one point just for logging in. He laughs when less than 20% of the class gets the question right. I would personally not take him again, though I do know people who are doing quite well in the class. If you take him, sit up front, pay attention, take a lot of notes, and understand that the content is hard enough with a good teacher.

Dr. Griffith was a great and engaging teacher, the course is just incredibly challenging and requires a lot of effort outside of the classroom. She made it clear that the course has a lot of material which required us to review the textbook because there was not enough class time. Dr. Griffith provided a lot of opportunities for us to succeed and was always open to any of our questions, even if it meant reiterating a small portion of the lecture during office hours. This class is just a difficult but if you prepare how she recommends and with the extensive amount of resources she offers, you should be fine. If you can, I would definitely take her for chem 135.

Horrible professor. I took AP Chem in high school and did pretty good in that course, so I came into this class hoping that the bad reviews weren't relavent to me. I was so wrong. She has a very odd way of teaching that doesn't work for anyone, and all the practice problems she does during lecture are so scrambled due to her disorganization that you leave every lecture feeling more confused then when you entered. Most people have stopped going to lecture and would rather teach themselves the material, and honestly that might be a better use of your time. Also, the homework website she uses, ALEKS, is hell. It takes absolutely forever to get the weeks modules done and you don't learn anything because all it teaches you is how to be frustrated. The averages for the tests have all been in the 40's (except for the first test but that one was very very basic chemistry). If you can take absolutely anyone else, or find a good tutor/TA that can help out. The TA is a very good teacher (not to mention funny) and will work with you to work through the problems.

I absolutely hated chemistry going into her class, but the way she taught it made sense and connected well to real world applications. The course is tricky, but as long as you do a bit of work outside of class you can keep up. She also knows the textbook very well (duh) so she could easily refer you to parts of the book for more information. Dr. Griffith definitely wanted every student to do well, and she did her best to make that happen - office hours are helpful and in class presentations are good. I know a few people who were in a different class for 135, and they all had a much harder time than I did. There are also lots of opportunities for bonus points.
Difficult work, but WAY better than other chem profs. Lectures give all info needed. She does require that you buy her electronic textbook for homeworks, which is a lil bit annoying.

I think he is a good professor for such a hard topic and crammed into such a small time, but he kind of reads off of the slides like he is seing them for the first time on the lectures, but his discussions is where he shines. He is very good in discussion and talks like he knows the content on the back of his hand.

Dr. V is alright. I would say that he is sometimes rude. I took AP chemistry in highschool and honors chemistry and he genuinely didnt go over some concepts I learned there but also a lot of concepts are so random on our midterms that werent covered (???) also, it was so bad because I am out of state he put the last midterm on the day before thanksgiving break. Barely could enjoy myself. Not necessarily his fault but comparing other chem135 classes they were having their exams earlier so they didnt run into the problem. I would study the midterms but dont just think that you will immediately pass doing so. He likes the throw fun surprises (bc again hes not that nice). Not only that but he will stand there and roast these poor students by having a graph of the grades from midterms. Then he will say “study harder” which honestly made me sad because i know chemistry is hard for people and he knows what hes doing lol. He basically makes it look like its all your fault. I studied, but even with my prior experience it was a hard class. Griffith is better but you will have quizzes every week. Not sure if thats what you want but there arent many options for professors. Dr. V is just ok. Hes not horrifying but hes not amazing.

Avoid Dr. Vedernikov for CHEM135 unless you are already knowledgeable in AP-level chemistry and/or plan to mostly self-study the course. His lectures are monotonous, hard to follow, and do not cover several concepts in the curriculum and on exams. All examples are written on a whiteboard in the front of the class that is illegible to virtually the entire lecture hall. He refuses to make exceptions for issues students may have, especially with technology (and the $80 often broken online textbook and homework system you will need to buy). Vedernikov is also often sarcastic and rude towards students who have genuine questions, brushing off his failing exam averages by suggesting that students "study harder." While he does provide full-length practice exams with solutions, the exams you will take often will contain concepts that were not on any review material and not discussed at all in lecture or discussion. Dr. Vedernikov very much treats this class like a "weed out" and seems to have no investment whatsoever in wanting students to pass or understand any course material.

If I could give Mignerey 0 stars, I would. She is honestly the worst professor you could ever take. Coming into her class I was optimistic that my general understanding of chemistry topics would come in handy, although, after trying to understand her lectures, I was even more confused. DO NOT TAKE HER. Even if it means you have to put off chem another semester, FIND SOMEONE ELSE! She can't lecture and the example problems she tries to do make absolutely no sense because she fails to explain them properly. The averages on the midterms were about 40% every time and that should say something to how truly terrible she is as a professor. She also has no regard for her students as she changes due dates of homework at the drop of a dime (not in your benefit) while the homework already takes about 15-20 hours per week to complete. As I have said before, DO NOT TAKE HER if you want to have any sanity left by the end of the semester or have a passing grade.

Dr.V is not horrible. Lectures were boring and honestly did not help at all. The clicker questions can be done remotely if you get the code at the beginning of the year. The midterms were not horrible as long as you studied. The midterms were very similar to the practice exams that he gave except for the 3rd one. Most people stop going to lectures or leave before the clicker question which is valid. Overall, not the greatest teacher but if you put in some work you'll do decent in the class. He sometimes takes jabs at students and sometimes doesn't answer questions in lecture but other than that he was pretty pleasant. Not the best teacher but way better than Alice.
DO NOT TAKE ALICE!!!!!! I hadn't learned chem since 10th grade so I knew nothing going in and her lectures only made it worse. I needed two separate tutors to get me through this class.
She is by FAR the best Chem Prof. on this campus, she gives an insane amount of extra credit which acts as a curve, 10/10

Easily the best professor you can take for CHEM135. Her course is very well laid out, the textbook used in class is written by her and has homework embedded within it. Her lectures are very interactive as well and she offers so many bonus points it's almost as if she's spoiling us. The work done on homeworks and exams obviously isn't easy but she sets up her students to succeed. She provides exam layouts and past exams before every exam as well. Going into this class I never expected myself to get an A but here we are now.

CHEM135 is a tough class but griffith will literally make sure you pass as long as you put in effort, even if you aren’t understanding the material well. Her online textbook is expensive but it’s very easy to read and navigate (isn’t structured like a traditional textbook). So so many bonus points, I averaged a 60% between the 3 midterms and still ended with a B from the amount of bonus opportunities. Very lighthearted person as well, she would randomly tell us stories about her husband and kids and joked around in class to lighten the mood. She should honestly be the only one teaching this class but if you’re deciding between griffith and someone else, choose griffith.

I am expecting a high A on the final exam. Many have difficulty with his teaching, but the same people do not attend the lectures and do not do the homework. As long as you follow course work and textbook and complete the adaptive follow-ups, you will be on track to do well in this class. Professor Vedernikov is a lovely sugar baby boo, and will give you full credit if you spend the right amount of time (only about 4ish hours a day for the homework, maybe a little more for the test weeks). Great professor and amazing mentor, would highly recommend.

CHEM135 is a hard class in the first place, and taking it with Vedernikov definitely didn't help with that. I didn't learn anything from his lectures and pretty much had to teach the entire course to myself. He has a very thick accent and a bit of a slur that makes it hard to understand what he's saying. You can tell he's a nice guy (I met with him once outside of class and he was very kind), but he's just not a good professor for this class.

His practice exams are somewhat useful; the first two ended up being very similar to the actual test, but the third one was completely different. We'll see how the final goes. A lot of people ended up just studying the practice exams, which is why the 3rd midterm had by far the lowest average.

He isn't the worst for CHEM135 (that would be Mignerey), but I wouldn't recommend taking him. Go with Griffith if you can.

I already had a decent chemistry background and I'm still struggling in this class. Averages on the midterms are like 40% and the homework will take HOURS. I have no idea what the curve will be, and as of right now (the final is in like 2 hours) I have a C, so I don't know what my final grade will be in the slightest. Her slides are impossible to understand, and somehow the lectures are even more confusing. She makes a lot of mistakes and sometimes she'll skip over a problem or slide because she's confused. She seems like a genuinely nice and funny woman in person, but please take Griffith if you can. I don't know if this is helpful or not, but she did tell us that the average will get you a C+/B- after the curve and she will not let a C- go below a 50. So... yeah good luck!

Horrific, one of, if not, the worst professor and class I have ever experienced. I did not even do particularly bad in the course, but he was so unbearable to listen to in lectures, his slides are from the middle ages. Horrific Professor, avoid at all costs.

His lectures are pointless and he adds nothing to the slides. No point in going except for clicker questions which you don't even need to be in class to do if you have the code, just have to do it at the right time. Only plus is he gives an old exam and answer key which can be extremely similar but not all of the time so I wouldn't bank on it. Your best bet is to use the textbook and his actual slides can be useful. Mostly just study the practice exams and do well on the homeworks.

He does not teach and just reads off powerpoints. Mostly a self-taught class. He will tell you it's your fault you're not doing well. There is a slight curve at the end. I stopped going to his lectures and just took notes of the powerpoint which he posts online. The practice exams can one similar to the actual exam, but sometimes they are totally different. The homework is graded on accuracy and you get two attempts to get it right. They also take a while, but it's only one assignment a week. Use the textbook to study.

Professor doesn’t know how to teach, I had to teach myself almost all of the topics for this class. The exams are hard and these take most of your grade so failing one can take a hit on your overall grade. Avoid this professor if you can.

Let me start off this by saying that I do not personally know dr. Mignerey and never spoke much to her because she scared me, so I can’t speak too much to her as a person, but if her teaching is any reflection of her as a person she is awful, objectively. The few good things I can say for her are that she will sometimes extend her homework’s to not be due over a holiday break, but the Alecks modules are such physiological torture to complete that this offers little help. Overall a great professor who cares about her students and is lightyears better than the other professors you can take. I was actually excited to go to her lectures. She actually cares about her students and is approachable during office hours. She makes chemistry engaging - this is coming from someone who disliked chem in high school. There is a quiz every week in discussion but all you need to do is to watch the prediscussion video and the questions are literally taken from the prediscussion video. It is a little annoying that you have to buy her textbook but her textbook is written very well and the homework is relevant to class.

Very easy. I like her teaching style, between switching from slides to written examples when needed. She's easy to follow however the material can get difficult at times, including the homeworks and midterms, however there are a lot of resources to use to study with and she hosts tons of office hours. Unfortunately a big resource is her own textbook which you do pay for, but that's fine as she makes up for this with the amount of bonus points she gives throughout the year. She also has a quiz nearly every week in discussions but they're never hard, and they're open note. The exams are tough but she does give a layout of the exam, which helps a ton and she allows a notecard on the exam.

If you're just trying to pass, take her.

Professor Collins tends to read off slides a lot, but his discussions are really useful and even though he does not do a lot of example problems, when he does he does it in a way to make the content easy to understand. Very fair grader and exams are not that difficult if you read the textbook and understand the content. If you have not taken AP chem before it might be hard at first but you will catch up to everyone else. He also allows you to bring a notecard for exams. One bad thing about professor collins is that he does not respond to emails.

Hi. Don't take him. I took AP Chem in high school and that was the only thing that kept me going for the first month. After, none of his lectures made sense. He seems to have no passion for teaching and laughs at the class when people aren't doing well. On the first or second class, a student had trouble with their clicker question because of internet issues and he said that since the student was in the minority, he had no obligation to help. Since he uses ancient slides to teach, going to lecture is basically useless and it has to be all self taught. His practice exams are good sometimes and bad sometimes, it's really up to luck. Be careful if you have him and make sure to at least go over the slides after lecture. Good luck.

I don't even know what to study for this class. His lectures are completely irrelevant to the homework and exams. The textbook (that you need to purchase to do the built-in homework) is decently helpful in explaining concepts, but at a point it doesn't help much with the specific math-based calculations on the exams. This only leaves the practice exams to go off of, but even that doesn't always reflect the topics on the exams (always be prepared to see something you've never seen in your life before!). He does not provide a list of topics that might be on the exam either, despite everything about the class already being in complete disarray. If you take this class, you will consistently be left to fend for yourself in a state of constant confusion and fear for what new topic is going to be on the exam, no matter how long you spent studying before. The only upside to this class is that he drops the three lowest homeworks (and the homeworks aren't too difficult to figure out on your own), and only keeps the ten highest clicker questions (which is a $35 subscription you need to purchase on top of the textbook fee).

You have to teach yourself everything, do not recommend. I took AP chem in high school and got a 94, but am struggling in this class due to the amount of information that he throws at you, without showing any example problems. 

If you do take this class I recommend paying more attention to discussion notes and example problems than the lecture, as they are more concise and actually give you practice with the content. Study old exams as well as your textbook. The textbook has practice quizzes, videos, and other good studying tools. Homework is a good chunk of your grade so try to do well on that (sometimes the discussion has the same problems as in the hw). Clicker questions can be done from your dorm in case you miss class.

Please do not take this professor. If you have to take this professor waitlist first, and if that doesn't work out, then I pray for you. He has a heavy accent, but it is still understandable; you can only see what is on the board if you are sitting in the first few rows. To give him credit for being nice as a person but still hard to learn from, he reads off the slides that those even barely make sense. You are forced to go to lectures because he mandates clicker question points WHICH YOU HAVE TO PAY FOR ON TOP OF THE BOOK THAT YOU'LL NEVER USE EXCEPT FOR HOMEWORKS. Grading wise, he curves like crazy, but if you are doing well to pass the midterms, To be fair, he makes the midterms really similar to past ones that he gives you so you can study off of those, except he did switch the last midterm to be completely different, throwing everyone off, which everyone failed. I stopped going to lectures after I got all my clicker question points and did well enough studying off the past exams except for the last one. Which had me very paranoid for the final. This is a very study by yourself class if you cant do that waitlist another professor or take it another semster.

Do not take him. Exams are bad. Not only that he takes away your happiness by giving the exam on the last possible date. It might sound good but when your friends and family are at home early for thanksgiving or winter break, you are still in your school trying to figure out the rate laws. Be careful. Stay safe.

Overall, Vedernikov is a wholesome and nice guy. He's just a bit old-fashioned, which causes his lectures and exams to be somewhat of a headache. I have nothing against his person, but (oh buddy) are his lectures boring. I know that what I'm learning is what I signed-up for, but I've found that learning on my own is just better. The exams follow the same format as his practice exams on Canvas, which is nice.

God awful. I can give him a break for reading the slides like its his first time seeing them because this was his first time teaching. But, his priorities are horrible. He canceled almost half of our discussions with no warning and when asked questions about tests or to elaborate on explanations, he failed miserably. On one of our exams I was marked wrong for stating that CH2S is a polar molecule. I brought this to his attention and he stated that I was wrong and when confronted WITH EVIDENCE he said and I quote "don't trust everything you see on the internet" and "I don't believe it is a polar molecule". That on top of his horrible teaching made my experience in this class hell. If you can avoid taking Collins do it. A teacher that cant realise when he is wrong and give me my one single point on a test should not be teaching. ALL OVER ONE POINT. This is pure speculation but I believe he missed a lot of discussions due to being hungover from going out on Thursday. He also didn't put more than half our grades in until the last day before the final. Also his office hours always conflicted with a freshman connection schedule or he just wouldn't show up to them. DO NOT TAKE HIM HE IS TERRIBLE.

If you are so unlucky that you have him as your professor, you are going to have to self teach yourself a LOT. He clearly knows what he is doing and loves the subject but is awful at conveying the knowledge to students. The only thing going for him is that most of his exams are similar to the practice ones he offers. USE THESE TO YOUR ADVANTAGE. I also recommend Organic Chemistry Tutor, you could literally skip every lecture and just watch all those videos and pass the class.

WAY WAY WAY better than any other CHEM135 teacher at UMD. Lectures although dry at times give you everything you need to know to pass the class. Her textbook and homework also help to brush you up on topics discussed in lectures. Although she doesn't "curve" the class, she gives so many bonus points to the point where if you got all of them your grade went up by roughly 10%. The goat of CHEM135, goat of a lecturer, fantastic human being, her teaching style is what I live for.

I would highly recommend not taking Vedernikov's class. He mumbles through an extremely cluttered slideshow where you are unable to sift out what is important and what is not. He never does any examples you will have to teach yourself the material. Sometimes he will write something on the whiteboard but unless you are right in front of him, you will be unable to see. Eventually, I realized his lectures were pointless and stopped attending. However his exams for the most part are fair, as he gives out a practice exam that is very similar to the actual exam.

If you have the option not to take him:
CHOOSE SOMEONE ELSE. (Someone else = Griffith).

If you do not have the option:
I am very sorry. To give you an overview of what to expect, here is the rundown on how his class is structured:
1. You HAVE to buy the textbook. It is ~$80 but it is better than the HW system Mignerey uses which is ALEKS. I have heard terrible things about ALEKS. I would suggest you do the HW and read the textbook to actually understand the content. Your 2 lowest HW grades are dropped.
2. At the beginning of every lecture, he gives "clicker questions." Basically you have to buy this thing called PointSolutions in the beginning of the semester and then connect to his session. During the session you are prompted to answer a chem question in 60 secs. Most of the class just googles or chatgpts it tbh. Your ten lowest scores are dropped. 
3. There is a built in 10% curve in the syllabus. So to pass with a C- you have to get at least a 60%.  
4. His exams are similar-ish to the practice exams. I would do it once or twice and then identify your weakspots. To get better in areas you are weaker in: 
GO THROUGH THE DYNAMIC STUDY MODULES IN THE TEXTBOOK. They cover every topic in the book and almost overprepare you. 
5. He tends to be harsh on people who fail midterms.... even if the majority of the class failed it. 
6. Good luck.

Final review: If you have the time, review AP Chem content over the break. I wish I did that :/

Not terrible. He is lenient with homework as the three lowest of thirteen are dropped and he only records 10 of your top clicker questions (you need to purchase a subscription for clicker questions, though). Lecture and slides are not helpful, you will have to entirely self-learn the course. First two midterms were very similar topic-wise to the practice midterms (but different enough for the average to be upper-60s/lower-70s). The third midterm was a curveball (not similar at all) that most of the class failed (he had to curve just so the average would be passing). The final was similar enough to the practice final, so the average was a 68, which is decent for a weed-out like this class. Everyone was paranoid about what unknown curveballs would be on the final due to exam 3, though. He does not provide a list of topics that may be on the exam, and nor does the textbook cover everything that may be on the exam, so you honestly just have to hope for the best and attempt to study everything even vaguely chemistry related.

This was the worst class I have ever taken. Mignerey does not know how to teach and the homework she assigns has no application towards the actual final exam or midterms. I spent 70+ hours on the ALEKS to complete the PIE only for it to not help my exam scores at all. The only good part about this class was the massive curve at the end of the semester. DO NOT TAKE HER.

actually the worst professor i have ever had and probably ever will have. exams are impossible the averages are always around 50% and the homework takes forever along with being irrelevant. 
the only redeeming quality is that the TA is a goat s/o Matt Wrotny.

Shane Collins is a pretty decent professor, which is good due to how much content there is in CHEM135. He goes over the content quite quickly but does explain things pretty well, which made going to lecture feel worth it. His discussion class is also pretty good, as he does over specific practice problems that we don't tend to go over in lecture. The grade is mostly made up of tests, so you will need to do good on those tests to get a good grade. His tests are fairly easy though as long as you understand everything he goes over, it's very rare that his tests will have a curveball. What I will say is it was rather hard to reach him, with him not responding to emails and having very poor timing for office hours. But in terms of being a lecturer he's a decent pick.

In short should you take Dr. Mignerey? Absolutely not. I'll start off with saying that I haven't taken AP Chemistry but took high school chemistry. For me, her lectures are fast paced and hard to follow leaving me more confused than before. I ended skipping her lectures around midway through the semester. The test averages were not good at around 50-55 percent for the last two midterms. The final exam was ridiculously hard. It was one of if not the hardest exam I have ever taken. The class average for the final was around 45 percent. If midterms and final exam test averages are that low a professional attitude would be to take part of the blame, but I got the impression that Dr. Mignerey was blaming it on us. At least on the Exam 2 test average. I also asked her questions multiple times and it seems like she gives me the "well obviously" type of attitude. I used the homework system ALEKS to learn most of the materials. At some point, ALEKS will more than likely burn you out because of how long it takes you to do. I'm talking about 15-20 hours a week no exaggeration, but it is on completion. Luckily, there was a massive curve at the end at around 20 percent. long and boring lectures that don't help with exam content whatsoever, it's more beneficial to teach yourself the entire course instead with the textbook. along with that, has clicker questions during lectures to make sure people show up. only benefit is a built in 10% curve into the syllabus (aka 60% is a C- to pass)

From a teaching perspective he does ok, his lectures are sometimes hard to follow but if you pay attention and go to all of them you will be ok. PLEASEEEE do not take this professor if you can. The average on all the exams have been around 50% or even less. Lectures are completely useless and incoherent. ALEKS homework sucks the life out of you for several hours, the only good thing about ALEKS is the grade boost from it. Matt should really just be the professor at this point. 

If you end up taking her, good luck.

His lectures are confusing, and his slides doesn't help. He teaches content that aren't necessary for exams, and overcomplicates a lot of the topics. I learned a lot more in 50 minute weekly discussions with the TA than his lectures that are twice a week for 1hr and 15mins long. Not many positive things to say about this professor's class except for that the exams are fair - ish. This did not feel like a 100 level course.

First, the professor himself is a good guy, but he just doesn't know how to make his lectures worth being at other than for the clicker questions. He started the year by giving them at the beginning of the lecture, but after realizing that everybody leaves after answering the question, he moved them into the middle of the lecture (not cool). His lectures are impossible to follow unless you're him. He moves fast and explores WAY too deep into topics that a lot of his stuff has to be decoded. I only realized that we were talking about electron orbitals (which I already knew well from high school) two whole lectures into the topic. Notes are hard to take during lecture unless you already know what he's talking about.

A lot of the coursework can be self-taught through the homework and some light textbook reading to reinforce understanding if you already have a decent knowledge of chemistry. The homework website (with textbook, it's all on the same site) will set you back about 100 bucks though, which is crazy. I would still recommend going through the textbook. If you're learning through the homeworks then they will take a couple hours each week. If you're entirely new to chemistry though, I pray for you.

Regardless of what other people said, this semester ALL of his exams were like the practice exams he posts, including the final. He will only post them if somebody emails him about it first. The exams have two versions, and a lot of the time one version was clearly harder than the other or could include gotcha questions. The course itself though is incredibly demanding in terms of memorization. There are a million things you have to straight up memorize like monoatomic and polyatomic ions, solubility rules, EVERY acid and base, etc. The exams were overall decently fair because he gives you practice exams, and the curve he gives at the end of the year to your final grade (85 is an A) is alright. 

Overall, if you hate teachers that can teach, take this guy for sure. If you already know chemistry or self-study anyway, you'll still not get an A. I'd give him 2 stars for the exams, but I can't bring myself to.

His lectures are extremely boring. He also can't help this of course but his accent does make his lectures harder to understand. The lectures do have important info but he often goes through hard topics VERY quickly. He also doesn't finish his slides half the time. I ended up going to lecture but taking notes on the textbook instead of paying attention to him at the end of the year once I gave up on him teaching me anything. 

So far, I've said nothing but bad things so why 3 stars? He posts old exams which are genuinely JUST like the actual exams. Often will literally be the same questions with different numbers/compounds. You do have to buy the textbook, but I learned very well from it. The home work each week also takes just 1-2 hours and is pretty similar to questions on exams (some is irrelevant but most is good practice). The final grade is curved heavily and it was in the syllabus.

Dr V himself may not be the best lecturer, but anyone who says the class is impossible or he doesn't prepare you for the exams is wrong. For exams one and two he explicitly tells you what you are expected to memorize. The old exams are literally just like the real ones. There's no surprises. 

I can neither recommend or not recommend him. I succeeded but it was not with his help. I also know some of the other 135 professors are even worse, so pick your poison.

If you are a self-respecting human being who doesn't enjoy consistent and prolonged suffering don't take this class

But if thats what you're into then go ahead and take the class I guess

He's a pretty good professor. If you like self studying, this class is for you! Go to class, sometimes is helps. When one door closes, another door opens. That other door is my goat Matt (the TA). Do the ALEKS homework, it will impact your grade. DO NOT BUY THE TEXTBOOK!!! The discussion homeworks are the best practice for exams as well as practice exams. All in all, please do not take this professor unless you are naturally gifted at chem.

I thought Dr. Stocker was a really good teacher overall. She doesn't like to be emailed but is a very friendly person and helpful when I went to office hours. I do also think she makes you memorize some things like ion solubilities that other classes get charts on for exams.
i love lascio

I'd highly recommend avoiding this professor. He mumbles a lot and talks very quietly so he's not very easy to understand. He's very bad at teaching and his lectures are honestly a waste of time. I love the dude. He’s a funny guy and easy to talk too, and lectures are fine. The only reason why I gave him such a low review is because of the final. Great professor, super nice + approachable, great with responding to emails, and pretty accommodating. He also is great at explaining the topics quickly and somewhat clearly.

FOR YOUR OWN GOOD, DO NOT TAKE MIGNEREY FOR CHEM 135 IF YOU CAN AVOID HER. I will qualify and say that I wouldn't wait a semester, I'd just get this class out of the way (even with Mignerey) but the whole process will be a struggle with very little in return. 

The first and most notable problem you'll encounter is that this woman couldn't teach for her life. I don't know where the disconnect exactly stems from, but she will go entire lectures making zero sense to anyone, using vague/unclear terms, all while speeding through content (she says we have too much to cover even though she can pick the curriculum and stuffed more content than any other prof by far). If you understandably have questions to ask, there's a decent chance she will answer in a scoffing way (I've watched her laugh at a question while answering one). 

Then there are the exams which aren't the worse thing in the world but are quite bad when the teacher can't teach. Honestly, the questions themselves weren't that hard, but you would get 50 minutes to answer 12 or so questions and a lot of the questions could take ~3-5 minutes so it was really hard to manage answering all the questions. The averages very clearly reflect that as the highest average on any of the exams was a 55% (the first exam) and exam averages only dipped from there.

The only reason anyone passes or has a decent grade is because Mignerey has an end of year "average-to-B-" curve. That just means that after everyone's grades are in, the average is the benchmark for a B-. On its surface this is honestly the only good thing about this course everyone can benefit from. That being said, the curve vastly underdelivers. The average for this semester was 55%, but people who got 54% went straight to a C- while those who got 56% got the B-. Additionally, its completely unclear where the benchmark is for A- and up: I was expecting and A or A- because my grade was a 71% and (despite being ~16% above the average) I got a B+.

The only truly good thing about this course is the TA Matt Wrotney. He is a prospective PhD candidate and genuinely an amazing, engaging, and funny teacher: I learned far more from his weekly discussions than I ever did listening to Mignerey ramble on. There were multiple occasions where I just asked him question after question and not only would he entertain them but also walk me through understanding the answer/solution. In every way, Matt is a better teacher and I wish he were the prof instead of Mignerey but he isn't and there's a chance you don't even have him as your TA.

En somme: Don't take Mignerey for CHEM135 if you can avoid it, she's an awful teacher with relatively hard exams and the only saving grace for this purgatory of a course is the curve and Matt.

He is a nice guy but teaches really fast and does not curve anything. How do you not curve any exams in this class... feels like he wants everyone to fail. Lectures are horrible. Only worth going to the first 10 because of clicker questions - through a platform which you have to pay a decent amount of money for. IDK if there's anyone else better, but he is not great...Just not that good at teaching, stopped going to lecture because it did not help anything. rough. too much content. insane curve saved my life at the end.

He is a really good professor especially when compared to other ones you'll eventually come across. He is super down to earth and a very nice funny guy. Cant hate the teacher, hate the class. He mumbles during lectures and you wont get anything out of the ancient slides. But every chem135 teacher kind of sucks. He is the best of the pack.

YES this is a difficult class, it's known as the engineering weed-out class for a reason. However, if you give a good honest effort you will be able to succeed. This is a very fast paced class, but as someone with no prior chemistry experience Lascio breaks it down the best he can in his allotted time and gives plenty of practice examples with increasing difficulty. The average for each exam is pretty low, around 65-70%, but there is a large curve at the end of the semester (For our class I finished with an 86 which was an A, I believe the cutoff for an A- versus an A was around 81-82). This is difficult material but if you are willing to put in effort you will do well. He has office hours twice a week and I usually went once every two weeks or so to ask questions, and sometimes he will drop hints about exam questions. The most important thing to do well in this course is to do the weekly discussion worksheets BEFORE your discussion section. Even though the TAs go through the worksheets, putting in this extra effort beforehand is the best way to catch mistakes and what topics you are struggling on. This also makes for a great review resource for the cumulative final, because you have written documentation of all the practice problems completed and what mistakes you have made in the past. The weekly ALEKS homework isn't too difficult but can be confusing and time consuming, but the actual discussion sheets are much more indicative of exam materials because he does not make the ALEKS himself, so focus your time on the review sheets.
Take him, he is a great teacher.

This course is very fast paced and challenging, but I don't think Professor Lascio could have done a better job. While he was a little misleading about how challenging the final exam was going to be, he was very communicative throughout the whole semester, and was very accommodating when he was asked. He's very good at responding to individual emails. Additionally, he ended up giving a pretty big curve, so that helped out a lot, even though he was kind of set on not giving too heavy of a curve during the semester. Overall, very difficult course, but he is the best professor to teach it in my opinion.

I want to make this short and sweet but I also want to start off by making a disclaimer. If you read through these reviews you can see a pattern between the CHEM131 and CHEM135 reviews. 

First I think the difficulty of 135 is already common knowledge. Dr. Lascio was one of those professors that I will never forget given I took his class my freshman year fall semester. He responds to emails insanely fast and is not trying to get you. If you go to office hours and show him you care I think you’ll do alright in the end. In class he actually explains and gives examples on the practice problems. Also a notecard was given on all midterms + final. 

The reason this was a 4 star review was because you’re in the dark for the entirety of the semester with Lascio changing his mind about curves. I was worried I wouldn’t even pass the class after the final but I ended up with a B. 

TLDR: Chem dept at UMD is terrible and I think this is the best professor for gen chem across the board.

Great lecturer who kept the hall of ~330 people engaged every lecture, but the class itself is so quick in its content. Some is easy, some is hard, and it really helps if you have taken AP Chemistry in high school, it's nearly identical with a little bit more content. You will need to study for every test, and pay attention very well in lecture; there is so much he talks about that doesn't end up on the lecture notes he posts. The homework is easy and an 80 free points, just do them and it's solid practice for midterms and the final. Overall good dude, but the class itself frustrates many people due to the amount of content and its difficulty. Great curve at the end as well.

Pros:
- Matt (the TA) is amazing, super funny and great at explaining things conceptually
- Curve is super strong, though its for a reason lol
- ALEKS (the HW) are almost free 100s because you can redo a question three times with three attempts each, plus it has a thing where you can look at how similar questions are solved
- Mignerey ends class early somewhat frequently, lowk whenever people start getting loud at the end she just gives up and ends class
- She decided to cut a bunch of material that sucked ass for the final
- She posts study guides with topics you should know or memorize for each exam, plus practice exams that are at least somewhat helpful
- The first practice exam was almost exactly like the first exam
- Discussion worksheets + GSS practice problems mean there is no shortage of practice if you need it
- I never read the textbook and it worked out fine
- You can trauma bond with other people in the class

Cons:
- She is terrible at explaining things because she just fucking doesnt
- You will probably leave the lecture hall more confused about the topic than when you came in
- She without fail spends the first 5 mins of every class having technology issues (ig that can be a pro too tho bc it means you can be 5 mins late lmao)
- Everything past the first exam was hella hard/different than expected
- She covers content soo fast, at some point you will be way ahead of the other Chem135 classes 
- Discussion will be pretty behind what is covered in lecture
- You need to dedicate a lot of time and energy to this class if you want to do well bc its a lot of self studying, + ALEKS take for-fucking ever (especially bc if you're like me and start them knowing nothing about the topic, learning as you go takes a long time)
- The curve is added at the very end (no individual exam is curved) so you will stress about what your true grade is for the whole semester

Mignerey is definitely an awful professor in terms of teaching, but she can be bearable with the curve and the extra resources. Try to go to lectures (if you are super dedicated and can have your own schedule of teaching yourself do that, but going to lectures was my only way of forcing myself to stay on track with the topics), definitely go to discussions, and go the GSS's and its exam review sessions if you can. Between her and other profs, I've heard its different but not necessarily better (they teach better but curve less, and also might require more memorization)? If Mignerey is convenient then it can be doable. You gotta put blood sweat and tears into it, but that might just be a feature of the class atp.

You can tell he's REALLY passionate about chemistry, but this course is so fast paced so you will need to be studying and reviewing notes after pretty much every lecture to make sure your actually understand what's happening. He definitely has an issue with pacing. He explained the first half of the course, which is significantly easier than the second half, in about 9 weeks, which only left 5 weeks for him to rush the last couple of chapters which are way harder to understand. He actually wasn't able to finish a chapter, but he did leave that off the final. The final was fulllll of info from the second half though. His exams are also extremely difficult, and the practice exams don't really match that. He is very quick responding to emails and can explain questions in depth either over email or during his office hours and is super nice. The class has 580 points total. 80 points come from homework. The homework has like three attempts on each question and 3 attempts on the entire homework so it's free 80 points. The other 500 come from the exams. Three midterms - 100 points each and the final - 200 points. He will say throughout the entire semester that he's prob not going to curve, but right before our final he did change the grade system to a 13 point scale. Also if you pass the final he will allow you to pass the class no matter your grade. He's a great prof it's just a terrible evil class.

Professor Lascio is a great and understanding guy. He's an engaging lecturer but lectures overall were boring and I fell asleep a few times. The day of an exam I felt horrible (probably due to stress and not sleeping at all cause his exams are HARD and I had been studying non-stop) and sent him an email asking if I could do a make-up exam even though I was not going to get a doctors note, expecting I would just have to tough it out and take it. He immediately replied and said to stay in bed. Literally was so thankful to him and I probably wouldn't have passed if I had taken that exam with a foggy head since I consistently kept a low grade throughout this course even though I had taken AP Chem in highschool. Also, once I showed my study guide to a friend with a different professor in this course and they had no idea what they were looking at- Lascio does go too deep into some chapters. The curve at the end saved me and I barely passed this class, though to be fair I should have studied for the first exam more and set myself up poorly. I also had no idea I would pass as one of my exam grades and final exam grade didn't get put in until after grades were due AND he didn't announce the curve until a few days after that. I wouldn't recommend him per se as the class average was around a 66.5% and many others barely scraped by, but if you put in the effort with him you should be fine.

Lascio was a great professor especially compared to the rest of the professors teaching this course. He understands that the class is difficult and tries to be understanding about it. The course is definitely hard and requires you to put in the work fi do well but it can be done. He also is pretty generous with the curve, this semester he curved the class at the end of the semester rather than curving individual tests. He gives out notecards that you can put whatever you want on but also makes the math based problems more difficult, If you do the practice problems on the slides and the questions in discussion worksheets you'll be fine. Also, if you are having trouble with topics in class or find that solving certain problems isn't intuitive go to the discussion, usually its just the TA solving out practice problems and answering questions which is a great resource if used correctly. Even if you don't think you have questions go to the discussion right before each exam since someone will have a question you won't know the answer to. 

He's also a huge fan of exception rules on tests.
In all honesty if you’re good with teaching it to yourself then she’s really not that bad, she’s very kind and her TA, Matt, is great. Aside from that she cannot teach at all.

Lascio is one of the better 135 professors. His lectures are pretty decent for the most part, although he poorly planned/paced some of his lectures. This caused us to fall behind at the start, and we kind of had to rush things/play a game of catch-up for the rest of the semester. Towards the end, leading up to the final, he skipped/rushed through a lot of material simply because he did not have enough time to teach us. His exams were pretty hard, and the sample/past exams were not the best at preparing us for the actual test. I would get high 60s to mid 80s on the practice exam, but would do terribly on the actual exams. Exam averages ranged anywhere from the 50s to the 70s. The class average was around 70% before the final. Homework was only 80 out of the available 580 points. There were 3 exams, each worth 100 points, with the final worth 200. You could bring a single index card to each exam, which had to be provided by him. Homeworks were somewhat hard and would sometimes stray a little from the lecture or exam material. However, he was very accommodating and understanding with deadlines. The final was absolutely brutal, with the average being in the 50s. Lascio curved a total of twice during the semester, once before the final, dropping the C- cutoff from 70% to 61%. After the final, grades took forever to release, but after he finished grading them all, he posted an announcement stating how he was dropping the C- cutoff down to a 50%. 

Overall, it's a really challenging class with a lot of material to cover in a short period of time. Lascio is a very understanding professor and is very easy-going and approachable. The curve saved me from failing the class, as I had a high-50, which ended up curving to a C.

Lascio is a great dude and is definitely the most effective CHEM135 teacher. He spends a little bit too much time on some topics, but I'm sure he'll get much better every semester. It's very clear he cares about his students, and he always sets his expectations higher than reality. His curve at the end of the year was very generous, and as long as you stay on top of each lesson as it is being taught, you'll be fine.

Best chem professor for this class, but the class is super difficult. At the end of the year, he'll curve the entire class (50% was passing for us), but during the semester, it's unlikely he'll curve individual exams. Approachable guy, super kind and fun to talk to, and responds to emails fairly quickly (unless he's busy with grading around finals or midterms).

Overall, I highly recommend him, but be prepared to study heavily for this class, especially if your chem knowledge isn't well defined.

Andrei has a heavy accent and mumbles throughout his lectures, which makes them pretty much completely useless (I went about two times total). That being said, the online textbook (which you have to pay for and is expensive) is quite good, and the class can be self-studied from that. He has a more than reasonable curve policy, and his exams are very easy (especially compared to the other CHEM135 profs). He posts old midterms in ELMS, and they are literally the exact same as the exams you will have to take, making it easy for you to know if you are ready. Overall, the dude cannot teach at all but the exams make up for it somewhat in my opinion.

If you have him, take advantage of the online textbook review option on the homework website it basically saved me when I couldn't decipher the slides and it basically teaches you the stuff that will appear on the exams, as the slides have a lot of filler info that isn't brought back up ever again. I honestly learned more during my discussions than during his lectures so kudos to the TAs. Bonus points for the practice exams being basically carbon copies of the next exam, but doesn't make them any easier though. Tip: start memorizing the required memorization materials as soon as you can, there is a lot you are required to memorize and if you don't it will bite you in the butt during exams.

Honestly he was a pretty bad lecturer (mumbled a lot and went very quickly) but all slides are posted to Canvas and follows the textbook (which is extremely helpful in my opinion if you choose to use it, it's filled with videos and examples scattered throughout). As far as exams go, he posts one or two practice midterms/finals before-hand for each one that's is essentially the same as the real exam (slightly different). But as long as you prepare using these practice exams and fully understand those concepts, there is no reason you shouldn't do just fine in this class.

I should be rating him 3 stars, but I want to bring his overall rating up a little. Also, it's sort of unfair to him, considering the course is the reason we all had such a miserable experience. During the first half of the semester, I was crashing out about how bad the prof is, but I eventually realized the material is just so bad anyway that even with a better prof, I still would've been in misery. Chem135 is not for the weak. I met up with him a few times and realized he is a real human. I feel bad for him. Yes, he's not the easiest to understand, and he sometimes assumes we know stuff that we certainly do not know, and there are many other issues (like the ones the other reviews point out), BUT he's sweet. At heart. Just talk to him. Make a meeting. Ask dumb questions and be as specific as possible. He will try to help. His heart is in the right place. All 4 exams were *extremely* similar to the practice. Put those exams into gemini or chatgpt and have it give you hella practice questions. Yes, you WILL need to study for this class like 25/7, but getting an A is possible. I also might be biased towards him slightly because (I feel the need to flex this - it's one of my greatest achievements) I was the only student to score 100% on any exam the entire semester (~350 students). So, it is possible. Lock in.

When teachers say “in my 20 years of teaching I’ve never had a class this bad,” this was the first class where I genuinely wondered if the professor was thinking that about us… except the problem definitely wasn’t us.

Never in my 20 years of being a student have I had a professor who manages to struggle with every aspect of teaching at once.

She can’t teach because she doesn’t explain concepts.
She can’t teach because you somehow leave lecture **more confused** than when you walked in.
She can’t teach because half the class is spent fighting with technology.
She can’t teach because the slides look like they were written mid-earthquake.

Numbers appear out of nowhere, steps disappear, and by the time you finish writing the first line of the problem she’s already on the final answer with no explanation of how we got there.

At some point most people in the class realized the real class wasn’t lecture — it was self-teaching through the textbook, YouTube, and discussion sections.

There was even a moment during the semester when class was interrupted due to a her having a heart attack, which gave me false hope for a second thaat God was delivering us from her. But to make everyone's week worse she unfortunatly was there the following lecture(worst day ever).

The ONLY reason anyone survives this class is because of Matt, the TA. Matt is genuinely one of the best TAs I’ve ever had. He actually explains concepts clearly, answers questions, and somehow reteaches the entire lecture in a way that finally makes sense.

If negative stars were allowed, I’d probably use them. The only reason this review is a 1 instead of a negative rating is because Matt absolutely carried the entire course.

He usually reads off the slides, but when you ask him questions, he really explains things in a lot of detail. Office hours are really helpful if you're stuck on questions. The class itself is not bad as long as you do the homework problems and practice tests. Usually, 90% of the test is something you've seen before, and the rest is conceptual stuff you need to figure out. The averages for the tests were in the mid 70s, but if you do the problems, you should do pretty good on these tests. CHEM135 overall is not that bad, and I actually enjoyed it despite my dislike for chemistry because Shane does a good job connecting concepts to real-life examples, making the class engaging. Try to take any professor who uses the "General Chemistry for Engineers" book, since that is easier, and the textbook is actually helpful and not pages upon pages of random information.

Dr. Lascio is definitely a 5 star professor, but CHEM 135 is definitely not a 5 star course. Even so, I've heard nightmare stories about some of the other professors who teach this class, so Lascio is probably your best bet if you need to take 135. He makes significant effort to connect with the students and make the absolutely terrible class as entertaining as it can be. If you don't have to take CHEM 135 definitely don't take it, but if you do, you should take it with Dr. Lascio.

Big V gets a lot of hate, but lowkey, he is a nice guy. He tries his best to teach, but his lectures are kind of boring and monotone. Midterms are VERY EASY if you study. I got 80s or higher on all of them. His practice exams are nearly identical to the exams, and the final was pretty easy with some studying. He is a nice guy, and if you go to his office hours or talk to him after class, he really wants you to succeed. The clickers are lame, yeah, but it's free points and not the worst. You have to study a LOT, yes. But it's a weed-out class for a reason, and Big V tries his best. TAs are great, Pierce was the GOAT. Really helpful for study sessions and providing practice in discussions. Average lecturer for chemistry, pretty average for CHEM135. Could be a heck of a lot worse. (DO NOT TAKE MIGNEREY!)
